theory: Qualify the missing-factor and missing-divisor rules for zero cases. A missing factor is uniquely determined by division only when the known factor is nonzero; a missing divisor is determined by dividend divided by quotient only when the quotient is nonzero, and every divisor must be nonzero. For example, a zero dividend and zero quotient do not determine a unique divisor.
